labelInUi: Reference tables — capability states are honest, including the ones that are not available

phases.label: Phase 1, week 1
phases.what: Observation only. Add AGENTS.md, one specification, and one read-only agentic workflow with safe outputs.
phases.changes: Nothing merges differently. No policy is enforced yet.
phases.exit: The team has seen what the agent writes for a full week.

phases.label: Phase 2, week 2
phases.what: Turn the checks that already exist into required checks, add CODEOWNERS and a ruleset. Then, and only then, choose an execution surface.
phases.changes: Merges now require evidence and an attributed approval.
phases.exit: A pull request has merged through required checks and a code-owner review.

dispositions.label: Migrate
dispositions.when: Active development with existing tests. The loop is worth most where evidence already exists.
dispositions.cost: One-off history import and pipeline translation.

dispositions.label: Mirror
dispositions.when: Something other teams depend on, while it is being assessed.
dispositions.cost: Two sources of truth for a bounded period. Pick which side is writable and say so out loud.

dispositions.label: Leave in place
dispositions.cost: None. Not everything needs to move.

axisNote: Phases are periods of time inside the pilot. Dispositions are decisions about individual repositories and have nothing to do with the calendar. Conflating them is the most common way this plan gets misread.

costLines.label: GitHub Actions minutes
costLines.what: Every workflow run consumes Actions minutes. Public repositories run free on standard runners; private repositories draw on the plan's included minutes and then bill per minute.
costLines.boundable: Yes, because the pilot is one repository.

costLines.label: Copilot AI credits
costLines.what: The Copilot-powered agentic workflows consume Copilot AI credits. Every workflow in this repository declares max-ai-credits, so the ceiling is in the file rather than in an invoice.
costLines.boundable: Yes, because the cap is declared per workflow.

costLines.label: GitHub Advanced Security licensing
costLines.what: On public repositories, code scanning, secret scanning and dependency review are available without an Advanced Security licence. On private repositories these fall under GitHub Advanced Security, where code security and secret protection are licensed separately.
costLines.boundable: Confirm with your account team for your plan rather than quoting a number from a slide.
costLines.citation: GitHub Docs, GitHub Advanced Security billing and features. Verify current terms at the time of the pilot.

pilotAsk.decision: Whether the evidence trail is worth extending to a second repository. Not which agent to standardise on: that decision stays reversible.

coexistence.premise: Work management and engineering evidence are different systems of record. They do not have to be the same product, and forcing them together is a migration risk with no engineering payoff.

keeps: Reporting that the business already reads
jira.gains: Engineering evidence is linked from the ticket instead of retyped into it.
jira.mechanism: Commit and pull request references carry the ticket key. Jira's GitHub integration shows the branch, the pull request, and the deployment against the ticket.

holds: Durable intent close to the code
github.why: An agent works from the repository. Intent that lives outside the repository has to be copied into it, and a copy is where accuracy is lost.

coexistence.tone: Atlassian tooling is not the problem here. The question is where engineering evidence lives, not which vendor wins.

migrationPath.premise: Migration is a per-repository decision, taken repository by repository using the dispositions above. There is no single switch and no numbered wave plan.
migrationPath.cloudNeutral: Nothing in this path requires a particular hosting provider or cloud. The primitives are the same wherever the workload runs.
migrationPath.pipelineNote: Assess pipeline definitions before moving anything. gh actions-importer audits Bitbucket Pipelines and other systems and translates most of the mechanical shape. The security posture in this repository is the part worth rewriting by hand rather than importing.
migrationPath.sequencing: During the pilot, no repository moves at all. Dispositions are assigned afterwards, on evidence.

Turn on the deterministic checks that already exist and make them required.
Add CODEOWNERS so an approval means something.
